title: AI-assisted cardiac measurements show an in-hospital mortality association
summary: In the retrospective international WASE-COVID cohort, left-ventricular longitudinal strain was associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment. Left-ventricular measurements combined machine-learned software output with two blinded human reads. This is a selected-cohort association, not an AI-only mortality predictor or demonstrated clinical benefit.
organization: University of Chicago; MedStar Health Research Institute; Ultromics

evidence.tested: 870 hospitalized patients at13 centers;722 had usable left-ventricular analysis. Final measurements averaged one automated and two blinded human reads. Adjusted strain association OR1.179,95%CI1.045–1.358.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective first-wave population selected for clinically indicated echocardiograms; variable missing views and same-cohort stepwise adjustment. 89 missing two-chamber measurements imputed. No locked external mortality evaluation; individual strain discrimination limited. Right-ventricular measures used a separate semiautomated package. Software architecture/training supplement uninspected.
evidence.ai_role: Previously learned commercial algorithms generated ventricular volumes, ejection fraction and strain used with human reads in the association analysis. Conventional regression estimated the association.

source_review.scope: Actual primary Methods/Results/limitations and both linked letters read in supported Chrome. Letters debate interpretation and utility; response clarifies odds ratios and all-cause in-hospital death, not PPV or COVID-specific death.
